Understanding Deterministic Builds

Deterministic builds are a foundational technique for making software supply chains verifiable, because two independent parties can rebuild the exact same artifact from the exact same source and compare the resulting bytes for an exact match.

One important detail is link handling: authors frequently reference other pages using relative paths, and those need to be rewritten against the page's own URL so they still resolve correctly once the content is moved elsewhere, such as into an EPUB chapter file.

Anchors within the same document, like a jump to section two, also need careful handling so they keep working after extraction.
